_what_this_is: Arm 0 -- our v1.0. RSI-Jev's recipe on a Qwen3-0.6B backbone, run through THEIR code unmodified.
_how_this_is_run: scripts/release_train.py in the reference repository: --model pointed at the local Qwen3-0.6B, --corpus at the output of THEIR scripts/build_synth_corpus.py. No file of theirs is edited. The two adaptations are a model path and a corpus path.
_field_names_are_theirs: An earlier version of this file invented field names. run_arm_lib expands spec keys into ArchConfig / FitConfig by keyword, so a name that does not exist is a TypeError, and a name that exists but carries the wrong value trains a different arm than the one described. Every key below was read out of run_arm_lib.DEFAULTS and rsijev.fit.FitConfig, not out of the prose. Five things were wrong before and are recorded rather than quietly fixed: freeze_input_embedding, scorer_fp32_outside_autocast and grad_checkpoint do not exist; options_shuffle and lr_mix do not belong in fit_extra for this arm; and lr_head was 1e-4 against their 1e-3, a factor of ten.
_freeze_base: false is REQUIRED to reproduce v1.0, and it is NOT their default, which is true. Their control table in versions/v1.0.md section 10 records that every frozen variant stalled below the majority baseline: zero-shot on the frozen base's own logprobs 0.3775, frozen tower with a trained readout 0.4850, frozen tower plus the synthetic corpus 0.473-0.483, against a majority baseline of 0.5185. The released v1.0 is 0.662, which no frozen variant reaches. Their words: 'Fine-tuning the tower rather than freezing it, because every frozen variant stalled below the majority baseline whatever the head or the data.'
_autocast_is_derived: run_arm_lib computes autocast_bf16 as `not freeze_base`, so bf16 autocast turns on by itself here. It is deliberately NOT written: writing it would create a second source of truth for a value the code already derives, and the two could disagree.
_freeze_embeddings: their default, read directly by the function. Matches v1.0's 'all tower weights except the frozen input embedding'. Independent of freeze_base: the tower trains while the input embedding does not.
_grad_checkpointing: their key name, read directly by run_arm_lib. The earlier `grad_checkpoint` does not exist anywhere in their code.
_min_trainable_tower: their default, kept. With freeze_base=false it is a floor that catches a tower copied while still carrying requires_grad=False, and run_arm_lib raises afterwards if the tower's bitwise checksum did not move. Lowering it would disable the check that makes a full-parameter claim mean anything.
_lr_head: 1e-3, their DEFAULTS value. The v1.0 record's prose says 'head 1e-4 constant'; the code says 1e-3. The code is what ran, so the code is what this spec carries, and the discrepancy is recorded rather than resolved by guessing which document is stale.
_eval_batch_size_is_ours: 8, against their DEFAULTS of 32. NECESSARY, and the necessity was measured twice before it was believed. A control at freeze_base true completes all three targets at 32 with zero OOM, which on its own looked like proof that 32 was fine; that control removed the very thing that makes 32 fail. The necessity test keeps the real arm's condition -- freeze_base false, so the 8.88 GiB optimiser state is resident -- and at eval_batch_size 32 it dies with `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: out of memory` and writes nothing, while training itself completed and their own `tower moved: max |dw| = 5.007e-06` guard had already fired. The fault is the INTERACTION: neither condition alone triggers it, and both are required. It changes how many questions are scored per forward pass and nothing else -- not what is scored, not the metric, not the training, not the model.
_xattn_heads: their ArchConfig default. It is NOT among the 8 keys run_arm_lib names explicitly, so at the top level it would be ignored; here it reaches ArchConfig through the documented **kwargs route.
_fit_extra_note: Every FitConfig field run_arm_lib does NOT name explicitly. An unknown name here is a TypeError at construction, which is the good failure mode. cal_method is none so the checkpoint is exactly the model as trained and uncalibrated -- their released v2.0 and v2.1 use oof_head_scorefloor, and arm 0 is v1.0, which predates the confidence head. lower_layers_n is 0 because that knob belongs to their v2.1. NOTE: notes live HERE, at the top level, and never inside arch_extra or fit_extra -- those are splatted as **kwargs into a dataclass constructor, so an underscore-prefixed key there is an unexpected keyword argument, not a comment. That mistake shipped and surfaced only when the arm ran.

_reference.record: versions/v1.0.md section 2, and the control table in section 10
_reference._not_comparable: Their numbers came from an H100 80 GB on a pinned torch 2.7.1+cu128 stack. Recorded for orientation; never differenced against ours.

_ours.corpus: E:/2026-AI4S/corpus_rsijev -- built by THEIR scripts/build_synth_corpus.py: 6,977 cases / 24,320 questions, plus 437 adjacent-domain cases held aside so an arm can show the result does not depend on near-workflow data
_ours.seed_order: 17, then 29 and 43. Theirs judges the mean of three and fixed 17 as primary in advance; that order is kept.

_host_feasibility_measured_2026_09_30.peak_vram: 11,872 / 12,282 MiB = 96%, flat across a real 3-step run. It fits; 410 MiB is not a margin.
_host_feasibility_measured_2026_09_30.why_it_fits: rsijev/fit.py keeps weights fp32 and runs the forward under bf16 autocast, which run_arm_lib derives as `not freeze_base`. Their own comment records that fp32 activations at batch 16 used 79 GB. Same saving here.
_host_feasibility_measured_2026_09_30.trainable: 596.0 M with freeze_embeddings true (751.6 M total, 155.6 M embedding). min_trainable_tower = 100 M is satisfied six times over.
_host_feasibility_measured_2026_09_30.readout_tap: readout_layer -1 lands on layer 27 of 28, and every layer is full_attention. Theirs lands on layer 23 of 24, also full_attention. SAME attention type, which is what makes running their code on our backbone a reproduction rather than a rewrite.
_host_feasibility_measured_2026_09_30.host: 1 x RTX 4070 12,282 MiB; 32 logical cores; 127.7 GiB RAM, 99.5 GiB available. Their reference ran on an H100 80 GB.
_host_feasibility_measured_2026_09_30.if_it_OOMs: batch_size is the first lever and it is THEIR number, set for an 80 GB card. A CPU-resident fp32 optimiser master is the second and this host has the RAM for it -- but that is an adaptation and would be recorded as one rather than slipped in.

_known_blocker_fixed: An earlier version of this spec carried notes INSIDE arch_extra, e.g. `_xattn_heads`. Both extras are splatted as **kwargs into a dataclass constructor, so an underscore does not make a key a comment -- it makes it an unexpected keyword argument, and the run died with TypeError after the 2.28 GB model had loaded. Notes live at the top level now, and scripts/check_arm0_spec.py fails on an underscore key inside either extra.
